sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Celidon, also written Cellydon, is a place that turns up in the Arthurian stories. Just as the celebrated wood of Broceliande lies in Brittany, so the timber of this site in Britain crops up in several accounts, though its actual whereabouts is a mystery. A meaningful battle was fought there that ended in a win for the knights of King Arthur. During his spell of madness, the sorcerer Merlin wandered through that woodland.

okr.objective: Celidon is an Arthurian site whose woods appear in several legends.
